_comment: The token-payload COLLISION case, run against the same probe CEM.
`<Lib>.Values` mints ONE value per token identifier, so a token that two attributes
want to render differently is unrepresentable — exactly like the identifier collision
`Emit.guardValuesModule` already fails on. Here `Bar.mode`'s CEM enum mints the pair
Letting `Dict.insert` pick a winner would corrupt the loser silently: `Values.auto`
would write one attribute's string into the other's DOM attribute, past a type checker
that sees one legal `Value` row and has nothing to object to. So the run FAILS, and the
error names the token, both strings, and the fix (give one a distinct token NAME — the
map form's key and value need not match, which is the whole reason it exists).
